newsitem.title: USA: Anti-cholesterol drug battle eyed in Q2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Anti-cholesterol drug battle eyed in Q2 earnings.

text.p: Second-quarter profits for the nation's pharmaceutical companies are expected to be up by as much as 15 percent from a year ago, but industry analysts' main focus will be on a three-company battle to dominate the market for cholesterol-lowering drugs.

"The whole industry is smooth sailing," said HKS & Co. drug analyst Hemant Shah. He predicts year-on-year earnings gains of up to 15 percent after adjusting for the slightly negative foreign exchange effect of a stronger dollar in most overseas markets.
"Pharmaceutical products, both old and new, are continuing to grow with increased prescriptions, lack of much pricing pressure and continued cost-cutting," Shah said.
"The real wild card will be Warner-Lambert Co. because their cholesterol drug Lipitor has had much stronger sales than people predicted," he added.

Lipitor was launched in February and is being co-marketed by Pfizer Inc. In recent weeks it has captured over 20 percent of new retail prescriptions for the total cholesterol market, according to Warner-Lambert sales data.
"Cholesterol drugs are the real horse race right now and some people are expecting Lipitor to have sales of $600 million to $700 million this year," said Mehta and Isaly analyst Steve Lisi.
"Lipitor is doing fantastic. It is slightly cheaper and more potent at smaller doses" than Merck & Co.'s Zocor, and Bristol-Myers Squibb's Pravachol, he said.

Lisi said second-quarter sales figures will give a clearer idea of just how big a threat Lipitor might be to Zocor, which had worldwide sales of $2.8 billion in 1996, and Pravachol, which had $1.1 billion in 1996 sales.

Warner Lambert's stock price has soared from $75 a share at the beginning of the year to $141.75 Monday morning. It has been helped by expectations of brisk sales for Rezulin -- introduced in March for patients with Type II diabetes who already take insulin.
Merck releases its second-quarter results Thursday. Warner Lambert and Bristol-Myers will release theirs on July 22.

James Keeney, pharmaceuticals analyst for Rodman & Renshaw, said he had expected flat second-quarter earnings for Warner-Lambert but last month elevated his estimate to a 2 percent year-on-year gain based on sales of its two new products.
Keeney predicted profits of U.S. drugmakers would jump 15 percent in the second quarter, slightly higher than the gain seen in the prior quarter.

He said Pfizer's gains could approach 20 percent thanks to sales of Lipitor and other key products, including hypertension drugs Norvasc and Cardura, antidepressant Zoloft and the anti-infective Zithromax.
Merck & Co. could also hit the 20-percent mark, he said, from increased sales of Crixivan for HIV/AIDS, Fosamax for osteoporosis and Cozaar for hypertension.

First Call, which tracks Wall Street earnings projections, has a consensus estimate of 13 percent earnings growth for U.S.-based drug companies in the second quarter, and a 15 percent gain for the year.

Abbott Laboratories Inc. last week reported second-quarter net earnings of $522 million, or 68 cents per share, matching analyst estimates. In the same period last year, it earned $470 million, or 60 cents per share.
The company said worldwide sales of its pharmaceutical and nutritional products rose 9.4 percent from a year ago, while worldwide sales of hospital and laboratory products rose 4.9 percent.
